The Congo Free State existed from 1885 to 1908 as the personal property of King Leopold II of Belgium. This massive African territory was granted to him privately by the Berlin Conference of 1884 and 1885. Under Leopold's rule, the territory became a byword for colonial exploitation and atrocity: forced labor in rubber extraction, massacre, mutilation, and disease killed an estimated ten million Africans. International outcry over these horrors eventually forced Belgium to annex the territory in 1908 and assume direct control, though exploitation continued under Belgian administration until independence in 1960. The Congo was not officially a colony but a personal fiefdom. Leopold II acquired it as private property through diplomatic maneuvering at the Berlin Conference, treating it as his personal estate rather than Belgian territory. Leopold's sole interest was profit. The Congo's rubber and ivory were extracted through a brutal system of forced labor. Africans were coerced, beaten, and killed. Villages that failed to meet rubber quotas were razed. Limbs were severed as punishment and proof of death. Rubber exploitation was catastrophically destructive. The demand for rubber created incentives for maximum extraction. The Congo-Kasai region's economy was shattered. Disease, particularly sleeping sickness, spread as populations were displaced and concentrated. Violence became endemic. International journalists, missionaries, and activists documented the atrocities. E. D. Morel and George Washington Williams exposed the horrors. The Congo Reform Association publicized the crimes. Photographs of mutilated Congolese victims shocked Europe. Under mounting international pressure, Belgium annexed the Congo Free State in 1908, assuming direct colonial control as the Belgian Congo. This did not end exploitation but subjected it to nominal metropolitan oversight. The Congo Free State exemplified late-nineteenth-century imperialism at its most predatory: African sovereignty erased, resources extracted for foreign profit, populations decimated, and governance reduced to coercion and violence.
